item.title: French Polynesia Cabin Cruise: The Floating Boutique Hotel for Effortless Island Hopping
item.description: Imagine waking up in a comfortable suite aboard a premium catamaran. You stretch out on crisp sheets and wonder what spectacular view is awaiting you today. Will it be the majestic twin peaks of Bora Bora or the white sand beaches and tropical jungles of Huahine? You step on deck and sniff the air: today’s port is actually the vanilla-scented shores of Taha’a. That’s what life is like aboard a French Polynesia cabin cruise. Every day, you get to go on a new adventure. At night, you rest and relax in the comfort of a spacious cabin aboard a shared catamaran charter. For many travelers, the freedom to visit multiple destinations rather than be confined to a single resort makes a cabin cruise a much better option than a typical holiday on land. What Is a French Polynesia Cabin Cruise? A French Polynesia catamaran cruise or cabin cruise is a travel option where you book a private cabin with its own attached bathroom on a catamaran. Instead of chartering an entire yacht yourself, you share the vessel with a small group of other travelers. How Cabin Cruises Work The catamaran operates much like a small-scale cruise ship but with a personalized touch. Your captain navigates the islands, and an onboard steward prepares your meals. This vacation style eliminates the stress of trip planning, sailing logistics, and meal preparation. And since vessels are shared among travelers, cabin cruises are more affordable than booking Tahiti yacht charters . Why It Feels Like a Floating Boutique Hotel Unlike massive cruise ships that carry thousands of passengers, a catamaran hosts between 8 and 12 guests. This creates an intimate atmosphere, similar to that of a small hotel, except you also get to experience different destinations and activities every day. In French Polynesia, our cabin cruises are offered on the Bali 5.4, Lagoon 620, and the Fountaine Pajot Ipanema 58, each accommodating 12 guests. Comfort and Convenience: What Is a Cabin Cruise Like Onboard? Life aboard a cabin charter is defined by relaxation and comfort. Your catamaran features decks, shaded outdoor dining areas, and a forward trampoline net. This net is a great spot to lounge as the islands glide by. No jostling for sunbathing space on crowded beaches or lining up to rent gear from stands along the shore. You can get all the sun you want on deck, and the cruise includes the use of water sports equipment. You can step directly off the yacht’s transom steps into the water, swim, snorkel, or kayak to your heart’s content. Island Hopping Without Repacking or Airport Transfers With 118 islands and atolls spread across an area as vast as Western Europe, French Polynesia island hopping is all about discovering the unique character of each destination. However, having your base camp be a hotel or resort limits your options. It also means you have to go through a drawn-out process of getting there before you can visit each different island. Traditional travelers must pack their suitcases, check out of their resorts, take a taxi to the airport, wait in security lines, and fly to the next island, only to repeat the check-in process. Meanwhile, on Tahiti cabin cruises , you unpack your bags once on arrival. While you relax on deck or sleep in your cabin, the catamaran moves you between Tahiti and other destinations like Huahine, Raiatea, Taha’a, and Bora Bora. A Tahiti cabin charter eliminates the need for regional flights and ferry schedules, saving you both travel stress and vacation time. Space, Food, Privacy, and Seasickness: Honest Answers Before booking a sailing trip, it is normal to have a few questions about how things work on a boat. Here is what daily life aboard your shared luxury catamaran looks like. Space: Yacht cabins are smaller than hotel rooms, but they’re just as well-appointed. They feature built-in storage and ensuite bathrooms, with air-conditioning at specified daylight hours when you want a break from the tropical heat. Food: Your steward handles all the grocery …

item.title: Why The Bali 5.4 Should be Your Next Charter
item.description: The Bali 5.4 brings together space, comfort, and performance all in an impeccably designed 54-foot catamaran perfect for charter vacations. This yacht was built with a focus on open bright living spaces, comfortable accommodations, and plentiful outdoor spaces. With room for up to 12 in its six-cabin configuration, the Bali 5.4 is perfect for social sailing. Dream Yacht guests have the option to enjoy this yacht through a cabin cruise or when the yacht has availability outside of cabin charters, book it as a crewed yacht charter for an exclusive experience with family and friends. A Layout Designed for Living The center of the Bali 5.4’s design was built around bringing people together while still allowing space to spread out. Fluid flowing spaces from bow to stern creates seamless connection between the outdoor living areas, saloon, and aft cockpit. One of the most distinctive and innovative features of this yacht is the large pivoting rear door. It excellently connects the salon with the aft cockpit creating one extended living area and allowing for a larger conversation space. Another unique feature is the sliding windows that allow for more airflow and light giving an open air feel throughout. Forward of the saloon a door provides easy access to the foredeck. Here cushioned seats stretch out into the sun allowing guests to relax and enjoy the views while underway. While the aft cockpit provides a perfect gathering space for lunch or dinner at anchor with comfortable seating. The davits and swim ladder on the stern provide an easy access to the water for swimming. Then above there is a flybridge with a large U shaped seating area perfect for sipping a morning coffee with the sunrise or sundowners after a rewarding day of cruising. Forward of the seating area find the sunbathing pads where guests can lounge while taking in the breathtaking scenery of one of Dream Yacht’s incredible destinations. This Bali 5.4 provides so many areas where connection to the natural world and each other become possible. Find peace and shared experiences through innovation and exploration aboard this yacht. Take the Tour Comfortable Accommodations Below Deck The Bali 5.4 continues to deliver through its focus on comfort as we move below deck. Each cabin is equipped with queen sized beds, a private bathroom with a shower, and adequate storage space. Natural light and airflow are still features even down in the cabins; some cabins even have direct access to the deck. For large groups this layout is meant to give everyone their own private space at night, while relishing the communal spaces during the day. Guests get the feeling of home and settling in through these comfortable areas instead of the fleeting feeling of a hotel room. Why Charter the Bali 5.4 Space for Everyone – Roughly 130 square meters of living space allows for plenty of room to dine, relax, and enjoy cruising without feeling crowded. Indoor/Outdoor Living – The yacht’s flow from bow to stern and one of a kind opening door from the saloon to the aft cabin makes it easy to roam between the interior and exterior living spaces. Enjoy the breeze blowing through the yacht which creates a light airy open feel that connects you to the natural beauty of the surrounding world. Relaxation Area Options – There is no shortage of lounging areas onboard from the flybridge to the foredeck choose your ideal spot to enjoy the sail from. Now Newly Available for Private Crewed Charters When a Bali 5.4 is not being used on a cabin charter it will be available for a private crewed charter experience with a captain and hostess. This means families or groups of friends can experience the entire yacht privately, with a professional crew taking care of the sailing, itinerary, food, and day to day operation. Allowing guests to concentrate on relaxation and taking in the scenery from any of the comfortable lounging areas. item.title: Bahamas Sailing Series: Your Guide to Yacht Adventures in the Exumas
item.description: Welcome to the Dream Yacht’s Bahamas Series We’re kicking off our Dream Bahamas Series—a collection of blogs dedicated to helping you explore the very best of the Bahamas by yacht. Dream Yacht offers access to one incredible sailing destinations: the Exumas. If you’re dreaming of a tropical getaway that combines adventure, relaxation, and incredible wildlife, look no further than a yacht charter in the Bahamas. This is the first blog in our Bahamas series, where we’ll explore everything these sun-soaked islands have to offer — from iconic anchorages to hidden gems only accessible by boat. With over 700 islands and countless cays, the Bahamas offers an idyllic setting for sailors and vacationers alike. From curated cruising itineraries and insider insights to local tips, travel logistics, and can’t-miss experiences, this series is your go-to guide for planning the ultimate Bahamian escape. Whether you’re dreaming of shallow turquoise anchorages or charming island settlements, we’re here to deliver inspiration and practical advice to make your sailing adventure unforgettable. Stay tuned for more—and let the voyage begin! Why Charter a Yacht in The Bahamas? While the Bahamas are often associated with commercial cruises and bustling resorts, there’s a more intimate, authentic side waiting to be discovered. Imagine trading the crowds and cookie-cutter experiences for quiet harbors, vibrant local settlements, and the freedom to explore at your own pace. A private yacht charter lets you escape the ordinary and sail these phenomenal islands in comfort. Snorkel vibrant coral reefs teeming with marine life, stroll along untouched white-sand beaches, and dive into crystal-clear turquoise waters—all from the deck of your own floating sanctuary. Experience this family’s unforgettable journey through the Exumas, where they embraced the island’s laid-back charm and the breathtakingly blue waters. Discover the Exumas: A Chain of Hidden Gems The Exumas, a stunning chain of 365 cays, are renowned for their crystal-clear waters and pristine beaches just 35 miles south of Nassau. Departing from Nassau, this adventure takes you to iconic spots like Big Major Cay, home to the famous swimming pigs, and Compass Cay, where you can swim with friendly nurse sharks. Snorkeling enthusiasts will revel in the vibrant marine life at Thunderball Grotto, featured in the James Bond movie “Thunderball.” See the top excursions for this destination here . Many of these treasures can only be accessed by boat, making a yacht charter the best choice to explore these expansive waters. Learn More About The Exumas Charter Options to Suit Every Traveler in the Bahamas Dream Yacht caters to all levels of experience: Bareboat Charter : Ideal for seasoned sailors wanting the freedom to navigate the islands at their own pace. Skippered Charter : Perfect for those who prefer to relax and let a professional skipper handle the sailing. Easy Crewed Charter : Experience worry free sailing with a professional captain at the helm and friendly hostess handling full or half board meals. By the Cabin Charter : Share a yacht with fellow travelers, enjoying private ensuite cabins while the crew takes care of sailing and cooking. Planning Your Bahamian Adventure The Bahamas enjoys a year-round tropical climate, making it a perfect destination any time of the year. However, the high season from December to April offers slightly cooler temperatures, ranging between 82-88ºF. Low season is between August and early October, several restaurants are closed during this time period. Getting to the Bahamas from the U.S. is simple and affordable, with a wide range of direct flight options available. Major hubs like Fort Lauderdale and Miami offer quick flights — just about an hour — making it easy to reach paradise in no time. item.title: Revisit the Abaco Islands – they’re ready & waiting!
item.description: The Abaco Islands of the Bahamas – devastated by a hurricane in 2019, and avoided by tourists and travelers for years. It’s well past time to go back. As a long-time Abaco Islands sailing fan, I couldn’t have been happier to have the opportunity to visit these unique islands once again. Their electric blue waters, powdery white sand beaches, and friendly local culture hold a special place in my heart. It’s been several years since my last visit – over 5 years, and before devastating Hurricane Dorian of 2019. A Dream Yacht charter would be a great way to rediscover the beautiful islands of the Abacos. And I was eager to see how the islands had recovered and what the “renewed Abacos” had to offer. Traveling to the Abacos Reaching the Abacos, Bahamas is easy from Florida, with many connecting flights from Miami, Ft. Lauderdale, Orlando and more. I connected through Ft. Lauderdale, and the flight is just over an hour. The views on approach are spectacular, and you can feel the excitement onboard growing with passengers taking pictures from their window seats. At the small Marsh Harbour Airport, customs and immigration are a breeze and a few steps after I was greeted by a line of ready and waiting taxis. Sam was my friendly driver, enthusiastically sharing local hurricane stories and experiences throughout the short 10 minute ride. Schools, markets, government buildings and housing – nearly everything we passed was either fully repaired or entirely newly built. Including the Conch Inn Marina where the Dream Yacht base is located. Dream Yacht & Conch Inn Marina The Conch Inn Hotel and Marina is better than ever – entirely rebuilt but keeping its local charm and flavour, and complete with the new onsite Snappa’s Bar and Grill, where visitors can enjoy amazing local cuisine with a view. I arrived early for my charter and had a couple hours to kill, and I couldn’t imagine a better place to spend it than with the hospitable servers and a frothy island cocktail. Aboard my sailing charter, I was spoiled for choice when it came to exploring the Abacos. The islands offer a wide range of experiences, from snorkeling and diving to fishing and beachcombing. And with so many beautiful anchorages and harbors, it’s easy to find a secluded spot to drop anchor and enjoy the peace and tranquillity of the islands. Sunday at Great Guana Cay But the first stop was an easy choice. It was Sunday. Sunday in the Abacos always calls for a visit to Great Guana Cay. The island is known for its lively Sunday pig roast party at Nipper’s Beach Bar & Grill, as well as the “after-party” hangout at Grabber’s, a short walk across the island. The “pilgrimage” to the parties is half the fun, where you’ll meet with a steady stream of walking and golf-carting tourists and locals headed for the event. We found both venues (and all the shops and marinas in between!) fully recovered and in full swing with spring break revellers side-by-side with aged salty sailors and locals. It’s a diverse crowd and everyone is welcome. If the Nipper’s dancing and music become too much, a set of stairs take you down the bluff to one of the most stunning and tranquil pink-ish sand beaches you’ll find. Hope Town – rebuilt & refreshed You can’t visit the Abacos without a stop at the famed Hope Town on Elbow Cay, and it’s as beautiful as ever with pastel-color houses lining the harbor. This charming island is home to a beautiful beach, a historic (still functioning) kerosene-powered lighthouse, and a quaint village with shops, restaurants, and galleries. I spent hours exploring the island, chatting with the locals, and soaking up the laid-back atmosphere before retreating to the well-known afternoon gathering spot, Captain Jack’s, for a rum-filled “Jack Hammer” cocktail. There are no cars allowed in Hope Town, but plenty of golf carts to rent for exploring the island. It’s a great way to see the whole island and stop at local eateries and beaches along the way.
